questions.question: In computer architecture, what is the fundamental structural distinction between a Harvard architecture and a Von Neumann (Princeton) architecture?
options: Harvard architectures execute fixed-length RISC instructions, whereas Von Neumann architectures require variable-length CISC microcode.
Harvard architectures utilize physically separate memory spaces and signal paths for instructions and data, whereas Von Neumann architectures share a single memory space and bus.
Harvard architectures rely entirely on asynchronous pipeline stages, whereas Von Neumann architectures are strictly synchronous.
Harvard architectures mandate dedicated hardware floating-point units, whereas Von Neumann architectures emulate floating-point operations in software.
Harvard architectures eliminate the need for an instruction cache by streaming instructions directly from external main memory.

questions.question: In low-power digital IC design utilizing power gating (shutting down power domains), what is the primary operational role of inserting "isolation cells" at the interfaces of a powered-down domain?
options: To shift logic voltage thresholds when transitioning between different non-zero supply voltages.
To dynamically save the full architectural register state before power-down and restore it upon wake-up.
To limit the peak inrush current drawn by the power distribution network during power switch turn-on.
To clamp floating output signals from the powered-off block to a deterministic logic level (0 or 1), preventing high crowbar leakage current in active receiver blocks.
To act as a local decoupling capacitor network that suppresses substrate ground bounce during rail collapse.

questions.question: In computer cache hierarchy design, what is the primary architectural purpose of a "Victim Cache"?
options: To hold speculative instruction prefetches before determining if the branch predictor was accurate.
To buffer uncommitted dirty cache blocks until a memory fence instruction serializes execution.
To store blocks evicted from a small, low-associativity cache to reduce conflict misses without requiring a fully associative primary cache.
To act as a hardware shadow buffer that detects soft errors caused by cosmic radiation and alpha particles.
To log invalidation snoops broadcast by other processor cores in a shared-bus multiprocessor system.

questions.question: In pipelined and out-of-order processor architectures, which condition must strictly hold for an exception or interrupt to be classified as "precise"?
options: The exception must be detected and fully serviced within a single processor clock cycle.

The architectural state must reflect that all instructions preceding the faulting instruction have completed, and no instruction at or following the faulting instruction has modified the architectural state.
The processor must complete execution of all instructions currently residing anywhere in the pipeline before branching to the interrupt handler.
The exception must be generated exclusively by synchronous software traps rather than asynchronous external hardware interrupts.
The program counter is saved to memory, but speculative register changes made by younger instructions remain visible to the operating system.

questions.question: In advanced-node Static Timing Analysis (STA), why do modern methodologies adopt Advanced On-Chip Variation (AOCV) or Parametric On-Chip Variation (POCV) instead of traditional flat-derate On-Chip Variation (OCV)?
options: Flat OCV cannot model inductive wire coupling (L dI/dt noise) in dense interconnect stacks.
AOCV and POCV replace static timing approximations with dynamic SPICE simulation on all critical paths.
Flat OCV ignores temperature inversion effects, whereas AOCV and POCV model thermal runaway in standard cells.
AOCV and POCV eliminate the need to analyze multiple process corners and operating modes.

Flat OCV applies a uniform worst-case derating that is excessively pessimistic, whereas AOCV and POCV account for the statistical canceling of random variations across deeper logic paths and physical distances.
